currentManifestItem.title: Chern–Simons boundary variation and BF equations
currentManifestItem.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with boundary, $\mathfrak g$ a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra with invariant nondegenerate symmetric pairing, and $A\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak g)$ a smooth connection in a fixed trivialization. For an arbitrary smooth variation $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak g)$, the Chern–Simons first variation is

$$\delta\operatorname{CS}_A(\alpha)=2\int_M\langle\alpha\wedge F_A\rangle-\int_{\partial M}\langle A\wedge\alpha\rangle,$$

where $\partial M$ has the outward-normal-first orientation. Thus the boundary term is part of the variation; the bulk Euler equation is $F_A=0$ when variations are compactly supported in $\operatorname{int}M$ (or when boundary data make the boundary variation vanish). For $B\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak g)$ the BF action has first variation

$$\delta\operatorname{BF}_{(B,A)}(\beta,\alpha)=\int_M\langle\beta\wedge F_A\rangle+\int_M\langle\alpha\wedge D_AB\rangle-\int_{\partial M}\langle B\wedge\alpha\rangle,$$

so interior-compact variations give the equations $F_A=0$ and $D_AB=0$. No boundary condition is imposed by these bulk equations.

For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ fixed, the boundary potential current of $\lambda\operatorname{CS}$ is $\theta_A(\alpha)=-\lambda\langle A\wedge\alpha\rangle$. On a compact oriented smooth surface $\Sigma$ (with smooth boundary allowed), put $\mathcal A_\Sigma=\Omega^1(\Sigma;\mathfrak g)$ and identify each tangent space with $\Omega^1(\Sigma;\mathfrak g)$. For $a\in\mathcal A_\Sigma$ define $\Theta_\Sigma|_a(\alpha)=\int_\Sigma\theta_a(\alpha)$, and let $\Omega_\Sigma=d_{\mathcal A_\Sigma}\Theta_\Sigma$. The restriction to the flat-connection solution space, wherever it is smooth, is the possibly degenerate presymplectic form. Explicitly, on tangent vectors $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ it is the constant closed form

$$\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=-2\lambda\int_\Sigma\langle\alpha_1\wedge\alpha_2\rangle.$$

At a flat connection $a$ ($F_a=0$), tangent variations $\alpha$ to the flat-connection equations satisfy $D_a\alpha=0$. For an infinitesimal gauge parameter $\epsilon\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\mathfrak g)$, the gauge direction is $D_a\epsilon$ and

$$\Omega_\Sigma(D_a\epsilon,\alpha)=-2\lambda\int_{\partial\Sigma}\langle\epsilon,\alpha\rangle.$$

Consequently gauge parameters vanishing on $\partial\Sigma$ generate null directions on the linearized flat locus. If $\epsilon$ is field-independent, the displayed boundary variation is $\delta Q_\epsilon$ for $Q_\epsilon(a)=-2\lambda\int_{\partial\Sigma}\langle\epsilon,a\rangle$. Nonzero boundary parameters need not be null and can carry such charges when the boundary conditions permit them; no charge algebra or integrability assertion for field-dependent parameters is made.

references.title: Boris Khesin and Robert Wendt, The Geometry of Infinite-Dimensional Groups
references.locator: §3.2, printed pp. 184–186: complete first-variation calculation, Stokes boundary contribution, and presymplectic structure.

references.title: Steven Carlip, Quantum Gravity in 2+1 Dimensions: The Case of a Closed Universe
references.locator: §2.3, equations (2.3.2)–(2.3.14): Chern–Simons Euler equation and the classical three-dimensional gravity phase-space interface.

references.title: John C. Baez, An Introduction to Spin Foam Models of BF Theory and Quantum Gravity
references.locator: §2, especially the variation of the BF action and the boundary-term qualification in Remark 1.

currentManifestItem.title: Invertible triads identify zero-cosmological-constant three-dimensional BF gravity
currentManifestItem.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with smooth boundary and let $U\subseteq\operatorname{int}M$ be open. Let $V=\mathbb R^{2,1}$ carry $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1)$ and a fixed orientation, and let $e\in\Omega^1(M;V)$ and $\omega\in\Omega^1(M;\mathfrak{so}(V,\eta))$ be smooth. The $V$-valued one-form $e$ is a coframe on $U$ when each map $e_x:T_xU\to V$ is a linear isomorphism. Use the volume-form-induced isomorphism $J:V\to\mathfrak{so}(V,\eta)$, $(J(v))^a{}_b=\epsilon^a{}_{cb}v^c$, and the invariant pairing induced by $\eta$ to regard $e$ as the BF field. For a section $v$ of $U\times V$, define $D_X^\omega v=X(v)+\omega(X)v$. Define $F_\omega=d\omega+\tfrac12[\omega,\omega]$, $D_\omega e(X,Y)=D_X^\omega(eY)-D_Y^\omega(eX)-e[X,Y]$, and $g_e(X,Y)=\eta(eX,eY)$. Zero cosmological constant means that the action contains no term proportional to $\epsilon_{abc}e^a\wedge e^b\wedge e^c$. The BF action is $\int_M\langle Je\wedge F_\omega\rangle$, varied with smooth field variations compactly supported in $\operatorname{int}M$.

Its Euler equations are $F_\omega=0$ and $D_\omega e=0$. On every region where $e$ is a coframe, these equations are equivalent to the vacuum Einstein equation $G(g_e)=0$ for the induced Lorentz metric, where $G=\operatorname{Ric}-\tfrac12\operatorname{Scal}\,g_e$. The associated Levi-Civita curvature tensor vanishes there. The equations and the BF configuration space also allow degenerate coframes; the statement makes no four-dimensional, quantum, or path-integral claim.

references.title: Steven Carlip, Quantum Gravity in 2+1 Dimensions: The Case of a Closed Universe
references.locator: §2.1, equation (2.1.1), and §2.3, equations (2.3.1)–(2.3.14): the 3D curvature identity, first-order equations, and ISO(2,1) Chern–Simons interface.

references.title: John C. Baez, An Introduction to Spin Foam Models of BF Theory and Quantum Gravity
references.locator: §2, pp. 4–6: the classical BF equations and the nondegenerate-triad restriction for Lorentzian three-dimensional gravity.

Use the volume-form-induced isomorphism $J:V\to\mathfrak{so}(V,\eta)$, $(J(v))^a{}_b=\epsilon^a{}_{cb}v^c$, where $\epsilon_{012}=1$ in a positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal basis and the first index is raised with $\eta^{ab}$, and the invariant pairing induced by $\eta$ to regard $e$ as the BF field. For a section $v$ of $U\times V$, define $D_X^\omega v=X(v)+\omega(X)v$. Define $F_\omega=d\omega+\tfrac12[\omega,\omega]$, $D_\omega e(X,Y)=D_X^\omega(eY)-D_Y^\omega(eX)-e[X,Y]$, and $g_e(X,Y)=\eta(eX,eY)$. The BF action is $\int_M\langle Je\wedge F_\omega\rangle$, varied with smooth field variations compactly supported in $\operatorname{int}M$.

On a coframe region use the following curvature conventions. The Levi-Civita connection is the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of $g_e$, and

$$R^\nabla(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

For a local tangent frame $(E_a)_{a=0}^2$, set $g_{ab}=g_e(E_a,E_b)$, let $(g^{ab})$ be its inverse matrix, and put

$$R_{abcd}=g_e\bigl(E_a,R^\nabla(E_c,E_d)E_b\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_{a,c=0}^2g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad \operatorname{Scal}=\sum_{b,d=0}^2g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{bd}=\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}-\tfrac12\operatorname{Scal}\,g_{bd}.$$

The Levi-Civita spin connection in $e$ is the unique $\mathfrak{so}(V,\eta)$-valued connection form whose vector covariant derivative satisfies $D_X^\omega(eY)=e(\nabla_XY)$. The BF action's Euler equations are $F_\omega=0$ and $D_\omega e=0$. On every region where $e$ is a coframe, these equations are equivalent to requiring that $\omega$ be this Levi-Civita spin connection and that $G(g_e)=0$. The associated Levi-Civita curvature tensor vanishes there. The equations and the BF configuration space also allow degenerate coframes; the statement makes no four-dimensional, quantum, or path-integral claim.
